decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY records the É accent revision policy but omits the client's explicit designation of the approved accent as a locked asset.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Kenji,

This round feels like a couple of steps backward because both the Hero V and the second V changed again.

Unless I explicitly request a change, neither V nor the É accent should be redrawn, refined, or reinterpreted. From this point forward, treat the Hero V, second V, and É accent as locked assets. Carry all three forward unchanged in every iteration, with every exploration taking place around those fixed elements.

My earlier feedback also appears to have been interpreted too literally. I am not asking the other letters to copy the Hero V’s left arm. They should instead feel as though the same hand designed them: their proportions, construction, and geometric language should relate naturally to the Hero V while the letters remain original. At present, the two parts still read as different design languages.

The 2nd milestone has been released. I’m looking forward to the next round.

value_updates.revision_policy: Treat the approved É accent as a locked asset and carry it forward unchanged unless the client explicitly requests a change.

decisions.reason: The client explicitly requires the already approved Hero V to be carried forward unchanged in every subsequent iteration unless a change is requested.

decisions.reason: Locking the three approved assets does not alter the existing shared-terminal rule or any terminal-treatment attribute.
The source asset-lock decision does not freeze the surrounding letterforms; their separately stated architectural relationship is already represented by the existing same-message MODIFY.
The locked status of individual V-system assets does not change the current composition, kerning, hierarchy, or case-treatment requirements.
The asset-lock decision concerns approved geometry and does not change the deferred champagne-gold material treatment.
Locking the Hero V, second V, and É accent does not change the requirement for a wordmark-led identity without a separate icon or monogram.
The source decision preserves specific visual assets but does not modify the broader brand-expression goals or constraints.
The reference to locked assets describes design immutability, not a change to the final production-ready export deliverable.
